extracted.intended_audience: inpatient rehabilitation facility (IRF) administrators, clinical staff, quality reporting personnel, and EHR/IT vendors responsible for IRF-PAI reporting and IRF QRP compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for collecting, coding, submitting, and administrating social determinants of health (SDOH) assessment items and related IRF-PAI items for the IRF QRP, including item adoption/removal, timing, coding options, training, burden estimates, and reporting procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection at admission only
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS is finalizing collection of the new and modified SDOH assessment items at admission only because it is unlikely that assessment of these items at admission would differ from discharge; collecting at admission only mitigates administrative burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS cited commenter support that admission-only collection reduces redundancy and improves patient experience. Transportation was modified to admission-only beginning October 1, 2026; Living Situation, Food, and Utilities are finalized as admission-only beginning with the FY 2028 IRF QRP. The decision balances data needs with provider burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific SDOH items adopted/modified
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt Living Situation, Food, and Utilities as standardized patient assessment data elements under the SDOH category, and modify the Transportation standardized assessment data element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Living Situation, Food, and Utilities are finalized to be collected and submitted at admission only beginning with the FY 2028 IRF QRP. Transportation will be modified to be collected at admission only beginning October 1, 2026, with the FY 2028 IRF QRP. These items will be collected and submitted using the IRF-PAI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection through IRF-PAI patient interview ('hearing the patient's voice')
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposed and finalized collecting these SDOH items through patient interview via the IRF-PAI to increase the patient's voice and to ensure data reliability and accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS explained that obtaining information directly from the patient is more reliable than relying on previously collected provider data because the IRF may not know the original source, how SDOH domains were defined, or whether problems have been resolved. Collection via patient interview may also prompt conversation and inform discharge planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility in tool/vendor used (no mandated external screening tool)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS will not mandate use of the AHC HRSN Screening Tool or a specific vendor; the focus is on whether the information is collected, not the specific tool used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS clarified the proposed SDOH items will not require a new collection tool because they will be collected through the IRF-PAI. IRFs may use different methods to collect information from the patient, provided those methods are consistent with IRF-PAI coding guidance and defined lookback periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of previously collected data vs. direct patient interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters suggested allowing IRFs to use data collected in prior settings (e.g., hospitals, other PAC providers); CMS explained reasons for preferring direct patient interview and set conditions on alternative methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS appreciates shared EHRs but emphasized limitations of prior-provider data (uncertain source, differing domain definitions, unresolved status). While CMS prefers direct patient interview, IRFs may use other collection methods if they adhere to IRF-PAI coding guidance and lookback periods; CMS will use feedback to develop guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding response options for nonresponse
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed SDOH items include additional response options to capture when a patient declines to respond or is unable to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS encourages IRFs to assess all patients and select the appropriate response options (including decline/unable) for all SDOH assessment items, acknowledging the sensitive nature of some questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not skip Utilities when no steady place to live
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS disagreed with a recommendation to skip the Utilities assessment item if the patient indicated they do not have a steady place to live; CMS requires collection of Utilities regardless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS reasoned that patients without a steady place may be in temporary housing or shelters and utilities information remains important for discharge planning; therefore IRFs are required to collect Utilities to have complete information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to pediatric and adolescent patients
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS considered comments that SDOH items may not apply to patients under 18, but concluded Living Situation and Transportation (and other SDOH items) may be appropriate for pediatric/adolescent populations and should be collected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS noted evidence and practice examples (e.g., hospitals using AHC HRSN Tool in selected well-child visits) showing feasibility and utility. IRFs may collect additional information relevant to pediatric patients and special accommodations. CMS referenced the lack of a pediatric-specific PRAPARE version but acknowledged ongoing development efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collecting from patients with cognitive impairment
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS acknowledged concerns about IRF patients with cognitive deficits but concluded IRFs are accustomed to administering patient interview assessment items to cognitively impaired patients and can collect these data consistently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will provide training resources in advance of initial collection (e.g., online modules, tip sheets, Q&A docs, recorded webinars/videos) to ensure IRFs have tools to administer new SDOH items and reduce burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training, technical assistance, and standardized resources
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS will provide a suite of support resources to help IRFs implement new and modified SDOH assessment items and minimize burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planned resources include standardized plain-language collection instructions, step-by-step examples, a dedicated help desk, a dedicated IRF QRP web page (instructional videos, case studies, user manuals, FAQs), listserv communications, free data collection and submission specifications for EHR vendors, and free internet-based on-demand reports for compliance feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of Item 14-Admission Class from IRF-PAI
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS is finalizing removal of Item 14-Admission Class from the IRF-PAI effective October 1, 2026, but IRFs will not be required to collect/submit data on this item beginning with patients admitted on October 1, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: Item 14 is not used in calculation of IRF QRP quality measures nor for payment, survey, or care planning. CMS analyzed CY2023 data showing less than 1% coded as incomplete stays. CMS noted data specifications provide other means to identify incomplete stays and will monitor downstream implications and unintended consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) information collection requirements and solicitation topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the PRA, CMS must provide 60-day notice in the Federal Register and solicit public comment before submitting an information collection to OMB; solicited topics include need, burden accuracy, quality/clarity, and burden minimization recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS explicitly invited public comment on the need for the information collection and its usefulness, the accuracy of burden estimates, the quality/utility/clarity of information to be collected, and recommendations to minimize burden including automated techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden and cost estimation methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS described the methodology and assumptions used to estimate burden and cost associated with adding/modifying IRF-PAI items: time per item, staff mix, wage sources, fringe adjustments, composite wage, and resulting per-IRF and national estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key assumptions: each of four new items adds 0.005 hour at admission and modifying one item reduces 0.005 hour at discharge (net +0.015 hr); staffing assumed 50% RN and 50% LPN/LVN; median wages from BLS May 2022 doubled to account for indirect/fringe; composite adjusted hourly wage $65.31/hr. CMS presented estimated changes in burden hours and costs per IRF and nationally and responded to public commenters disputing the comprehensiveness of cost components (training, software, reconciliation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine item and measure monitoring and willingness to consider removals
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS routinely reviews IRF-PAI item sets to identify redundancies and opportunities to simplify data submission requirements, and will continue to monitor and consider removing items to reduce administrative burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will continue item monitoring, analyze downstream implications before removal, and consider public comments. Example: after analysis CMS concluded Item 14 could be removed without unintended consequences but will continue monitoring post-removal.
